div.head: VI Atr 10.3
div.ab: ⁊ geþence swyþe georne se þe oþrum deme, hwæs he sylf gyrne, þonne he þus cweðe: ‘Et dimitte nobis debita nostra’ et reliqua.
⁊ geþence swyþe georne se þe oþrum deme, hwæs he sylf gyrne, þonne he þus cweðe: “Et dimitte nobis debita nostra” et reliqua.
And geþence swyþe georne se þe oþrum deme, hwæs he sylf gyrne, þonne he þus cweðe: Et dimitte nobis debita nostra, et reliqua.
Und es bedenke recht ernstlich, wer anderen Urtheil spricht, was er selbst begehrt, wenn er folgendermassen spricht: Et dimitte nobis debita nostra u. s. w.
And let whoever passes judgment on others consider very earnestly what he himself desires when he says: ‘And forgive us our debts’, etc.
And he who judges another shall earnestly consider what he himself desires when he says: "Forgive us our trespasses" etc.
And the person who judges another shall reflect sincerely upon his own motivations when he recites: Forgive us our trespasses, etc.

note.seg: Cnut II 2a setzt deutlicher ‘Justizgewalt des Richters’ (s. d. Gl 1. 12), vielleicht im Ggs. zu der als vorhergegangen hinzuzudenkenden Urteilsfindung
Cnut II 2a puts it more clearly as ‘the judge’s judicial authority’ (see that word in Gl 1. 12), perhaps in contrast to the finding of the judgement, which is to be understood as having preceded
This clause is not found in V Atr., cf. II Cn. 2 a.
